newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US negotiator "pleased" with telecom pact progress.
newsitem.headline: US negotiator "pleased" with telecom pact progress.

text.p: A U.S. negotiator said on Friday that the United States was "pleased with progress" in talks on a global telecoms pact but declined to say if a deal was in the offing.
The negotiator told reporters: "There have been some very good offers put on the table...We are pleased with the progress."
He was speaking after a meeting at the World Trade Organisation to assess prospects for a pact by Saturday's deadline.
Trade officials quoted U.S. Deputy Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang as telling the meeting that he hoped a "critical mass" of offers would be on the table by Saturday for an accord to be clinched.

But European Union and other diplomats said the U.S. had thrown a new problem into the negotiations by saying it would take an exemption on equal treatment for all trade partners under the deal for some satellite and broadcasting services.

One EU official said this move had come as a "complete surprise." The EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan would be telephoning U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in Washington later for clarification, the official said.
Another U.S. official said there would be no question of extending the talks beyond Saturday. "Tomorrow is the last night. We're not going to go beyond tomorrow," he told reporters.
